_comment: Hand-written per-report digests for the Research Lens. Keyed by zsxq file_id (string). Fields: score (0-10 read-worthiness), why (why the report is bullish/neutral/bearish on the ticker), insight (insight density), data (data support), event (what corporate/news event preceded the report). Written from full reads of each local PDF; see reports/recommend/GEV_Research_Lens_Reading_List_2026-09-15.md and reports/recommend/Meta_Platforms_META_Research_Lens_2026-09-15.md for the long-form versions. Covers GEV and META (Meta Platforms).

214514824525141.why: Overweight, TP $822. GEV is a valuation page in a Siemens Energy note; the argument is the gas-turbine supply model — 2025 single-cycle orders ~88GW against ~50GW of supply, but capacity doubles to 75GW by 2028 and 97GW of gas by 2030, and GEV adds only ~4GW of small/mid capacity in 2028-30. Exhibit 3 shows GEV's backlog plus reservations at 62GW versus Siemens Energy's 70GW, so GEV is no longer the clear scale leader.
214514824525141.insight: The best negative evidence on GEV in the set, and it comes from a house that is simultaneously Overweight. Five explicit caveats on the supply build: MHI alone is 8.6GW of the 22GW 2028-30 step-up, engine GW is not all data-centre-reachable, and blades/vanes stay tight.
214514824525141.data: 22 pages, 12 exhibits. GEV itself is valuation-only: 18.2x 2028 EV/EBITA and 26.6x PE versus Siemens Energy's 33% PE discount.
214514824525141.event: Published two days before GEV's 4Q25 print (28 Jan 2026) and flags it as a catalyst — a rare pre-print framing.

415554212511288.why: Hold, TP $740, roughly 12% below the then-price of $841.27 — the only Hold among the overseas producers in the valuation comp table (Siemens Energy Buy at +11%). The negative is valuation, not thesis.
415554212511288.insight: A few sharp GEV capacity datapoints buried in a China-OEM note: capacity sold out through 2029 with delivery slots stretching into the late 2030s, an 83GW backlog at end-CY2025, and the 20GW to 24GW ramp. GEV is also the bull-case ceiling — Dongfang's aggressive case assumes GEV-like ASPs and margins and still yields only 30% upside.
415554212511288.data: 18 pages, 29 sourced tables and charts. GEV appears on ~7 pages as one comp row plus one pricing chart (GEV 5.0-5.5 versus Dongfang 2.0-5.0 RMB/watt).
415554212511288.event: Post-4Q25, which is the source of the 83GW figure. The trigger is Dongfang's early-2026 deposit for 10 G50 units from a Canadian data-centre customer.

585551114124884.why: Overweight, TP $1,000, with GEV named a top pick 'owing to backlog visibility, increasing pricing in pipeline, and solid cash flow/balance sheet.' The evidence is five bullets: backlog plus SRA of 83GW at YE25 (up from 36GW at YE24), global year-to-date orders +72% y/y, North America orders +160% y/y, gas capacity sold out through YE29, and ramping Electrification margins.
585551114124884.insight: A 2025-in-review recap. The 83GW, +72% and +160% figures are the entire GEV payload — no GEV estimates and no model.
585551114124884.data: 21 pages with ~7 chart exhibits over ~10 content pages and one GEV table row.
585551114124884.event: Priced 6 Mar 2026, about five weeks after GEV's 4Q25; flags pending FEOC guidance, Section 232 and AD/CVD tariffs.

585551445584884.why: Buy, TP $936 from $841.30. GEV is the re-rating benchmark for Chinese gas-turbine names: UBS argues Dongfang and Harbin should re-rate toward GEV's multiple despite carrying a 28-36% EPS CAGR against GEV's 16%.
585551445584884.insight: The additive piece is Figure 8's SOTP — Power EBIT $5,406m plus Electrification and Wind $2,989m at 20-25x implies 42-45x 2027e PE for the gas-turbine segment, with the discount attributed to 'the drag from GE Vernova's loss-making wind turbine business.' Also 4Q25 orders +79% y/y and the Dongfang/Harbin PE discount narrowing to 43% from a 52% average.
585551445584884.data: 45 pages, 27 numbered figures. GEV appears in Figures 8, 17, 19, 23, 26 and 29, but its Buy rating is asserted with no GEV estimates.
585551445584884.event: Post-4Q25, the source of the +79% order figure, alongside Siemens capacity news and US hyperscaler capex upgraded +59% y/y for 2026e.

585545825518884.why: GEV is not on the Conviction List — the April additions are Citizens Financial and Carlisle, the removals BAC and HSY — and it carries no rating, target or price. It appears twice as a supplier reference: Duke's GEV partnership and 20 secured gas turbines, and NVT's order acceleration against a value chain 'booking DC orders out to 2030.'
585545825518884.insight: Nothing new on GEV. Its only use is independent confirmation that utilities and electrical OEMs are still booking GEV-linked orders into the 2030s.
585545825518884.data: 75 pages, 35 exhibits, none on GEV. GEV appears in two of roughly 23 company sections.
585545825518884.event: A routine monthly refresh on 1 April. The macro backdrop is the Iran conflict — Brent forecast at $85/bbl and Strait of Hormuz flows at 6% of normal. GEV's 4Q25 was already out; 1Q26 came later.

415518585855828.why: Hold, TP $740 against a $991.30 close — about 25% below the market, with no estimate change, no GEV earnings model and no re-underwriting. It is a valuation verdict only, and it was priced the day before GEV's 1Q26 print.
415518585855828.insight: Oddly constructive on everything else: FOAK BWRX-300 at OPG Darlington targeting 2029 commissioning, TVA's Clinch River filing for 800MW of SMRs with a $400m DOE grant, SMR revenue that 'could pull forward' from a 2032+ base, up to $40bn of Japanese government investment behind GEV-Hitachi SMRs in Tennessee and Alabama, a 65-reactor installed base, and CEO Strazik's 5GW uprate opportunity.
415518585855828.data: 59 pages, ~35 sourced exhibits. GEV gets a full company page (p.36) plus the cover ratings table, but little on earnings impact.
415518585855828.event: Priced at the close of 21 Apr 2026, one day before GEV's 1Q26 — so the Hold predates the quarter it is meant to describe and was never revisited.

415248452524448.why: Buy, with no price target anywhere in the document. The GEV case is two sentences: 'Our estimates went up the most for NVT, GEV and VRT' and 'GEV and VRT are the most direct beneficiaries of our structural growth outlook.'
415248452524448.insight: Consensus-level and thematic. The only original work is earnings-season dispersion — AI-exposed industrials +14% organic versus +1% for non-AI, a record 45pp spread — with no GEV backlog, order or margin numbers.
415248452524448.data: 12 pages with no exhibits or tables; the sole GEV datapoint is the disclosure-table price of $1,062.95 on 1 May 2026.
415248452524448.event: Written as Q1 earnings closed — GEV's 1Q26 was 22 Apr 2026. Cites Google saying 2027 capex rises 'significantly.'

584251128411224.why: Buy with no price target; one of 23 'Top Picks to Play DC Supply Chain Tightness.' The case is that GEV's problem is supply, not demand: 1Q26 orders of $18.3B (+71% organically), total backlog $163B, and Electrification booking $2.4B of data-centre equipment in the quarter alone, more than all of 2025 combined.
584251128411224.insight: A proprietary six-constraint model with a 12GW 2025 delivery deficit. The sharpest GEV-specific work is on transformers — lead times beyond 24-36 months against a 13.2GW 2026 ceiling — where GEV's data-centre-relevant revenue CAGR runs 79.6% for 2023-26, and the Prolec JV adds share that 'is not fully reflected in forward estimates.'
584251128411224.data: 32 pages, 38 exhibits, two of them GEV-relevant (Ex. 27/28).
584251128411224.event: Post-1Q26, folding in the Prolec JV consolidation; written before 2Q26.

214524525528511.why: Overweight, PT $1,302, appearing only in a comp table ('GEV US OW 1,049 1,302 24%'). No rating rationale, no target derivation, no GEV earnings. GEV serves as the valuation yardstick — Yingliu trades at 29x FY28E PE, below GEV's 32x.
214524525528511.insight: A tight, data-rich supplier note whose GEV value is the demand frame: AI capex of $5.5T through 2030 (raised from $5.1T), data-centre power capacity raised to 138GW from 122GW, and global gas-turbine demand above 100GW a year from 2026 to 2035 against only 64GW of 2026 manufacturing capacity.
214524525528511.data: 10 pages, 4 exhibits. GEV appears once, in Table 2.
214524525528511.event: Between 1Q26 and 2Q26. The triggers were Baker Hughes' 2026-31 renewal, a Siemens Energy management visit, and a rotation out of AI-power names.

412424445241828.why: Outperform, PT $1,206 from a $1,045.17 price. The link to GEV is indirect — FERC Order 2222 and virtual power plants, where GEV's FLEXIQ EMS offers optionality. No GEV financials are used.
412424445241828.insight: Strong on the VPP and peaker theme, but the route from VPP growth to GEV earnings is asserted rather than modelled.

584281422521424.why: Overweight, PT $1,302, written the day after GEV's own 2Q26 print. About 20GW of new gas power contracts signed; the FY26E exit expectation for gas backlog plus SRA raised to at least 125GW from 110GW; 1H26 gas equipment pricing running more than 20% above 4Q25, with 2H26 at the higher end of the 10-20% uplift range; and a quantified supply/demand bridge — FY26 supply ~64GW against demand of ~115-120GW, tightening only around FY30. GEV also outlined a pathway to 30GW of annual gas output by 2030 from its existing footprint.
584281422521424.insight: The highest-density GEV read in the set. One caveat worth flagging: the Q/Q deltas ('gas backlog expanded 44GW to 53GW; SRAs increased 56GW to 63GW') do not reconcile with the 100GW to 116GW total quoted on the same page.
584281422521424.data: 9 pages, 2 exhibits — GEV backlog plus SRAs, and a 17-name gas-turbine component/OEM comp table.
584281422521424.event: Same-week read-across on the 2Q26 print, making this the most time-sensitive document in the set.

584285418514214.why: Overweight with the target raised from $1,302 to $1,330 in the six days since the previous note. The GEV content is about two paragraphs off the 2Q26 print: orders of $24.2B 'well above expectations,' the 20GW gas expansion complete and targeting 24GW by FY28 and 30GW by 2030, and FY26 FCF guidance raised to $11.5-12.5B from $6.5-7.5B.
584285418514214.insight: The differentiated value is the three-company triangulation — Bloom Energy data-centre orders more than 2x all of FY25, Innio data-centre book-to-bill of 6.3x with capacity to 5GW by YE26 — evidence that behind-the-meter demand is not rolling over.
584285418514214.data: 14 pages, 2 exhibits (AIDC power comparison; machinery sector comparison).
584285418514214.event: Six days after 2Q26, capturing a target revision in flight; also follows Weichai Group's 21 Jul A-share increase announcement.

584284828815454.why: Buy-rated only as a member of the Reliability basket — 'GEV GE Vernova United States 271.1 $1017.96 92% 69%' — with no GEV rating rationale or price target anywhere in the document. The single fundamental datapoint: GEV expects more than 50% of its 2031 capacity to be contracted by the end of 2026.
584284828815454.insight: A strong thematic read on AI power demand — 2030 global data-centre demand +170% versus 2025, raised from +117%; hyperscaler capex plus R&D above $1trn in 2026e — in which GEV sits alongside Siemens Energy, Quanta, Vertiv and MasTec.
584284828815454.data: 36 pages, 36 exhibits, none GEV-specific; GEV appears twice.
584284828815454.event: Written after the 2Q26 earnings call, which it quotes directly, and after a round of hyperscaler capex hikes.

412841521854558.why: Outperform, PT $1,298 from $987.46, backed by a primary procurement survey (n=50, ~40% hyperscalers). GEV wins more than 20% of power spend for 14% of respondents — 22% among hyperscalers — against Schneider at 64%, and leads the SST purchase-intent group.
412841521854558.insight: The only forward survey evidence on GEV's electrical share in the set — and it is mildly uncomfortable, since a 14% versus 64% split is not the profile of a share gainer.
412841521854558.data: 27 pages, ~30 exhibits; GEV's slice is three share bars and two SST charts.
412841521854558.event: About a month after 2Q26; no GEV-specific trigger.

214822528121111.why: Outperform, PT $1,298 — but the report contains no GEV thesis. Value capture in modular data-centre construction is attributed to Schneider, Vertiv and Eaton. GEV's only substantive appearance is Exhibit 17, noting that Bloom Energy has outperformed it by almost 150pp year-to-date (GEV +44% versus Bloom +191%), a price-return chart with no view attached.
214822528121111.insight: Highly differentiated on modularisation — a ~126GW credibility-adjusted pipeline for 2026-30, $0.9B/GW incremental PV with ~25% accruing to OEMs, a $1.9B/GW power-module TAM — and near-zero on GEV.
214822528121111.data: 57 pages, 81 exhibits, exactly one of which mentions GEV.
214822528121111.event: About two months after 2Q26, in the window where GEV lagged fuel-cell peers; no GEV trigger cited.

184445214585182.why: Overweight, PT $1,000, an Analyst Focus List pick following the 4Q25 order beat. The case is quantitative: about 16.7x FY28E EBITDA and 14.1x FY29E, a premium to peers justified by above-average growth, with an SOTP of 20x FY29E Power EBITDA, 16x FY28E Electrification and 6x FY29E Wind at a discount to Vestas.
184445214585182.insight: The SOTP multiple rationale is genuinely differentiated — this is the better of the two JPM 2026-03-09 notes. The remainder restates the grid-bottleneck consensus. Not shown on the lens itself: the ticker/broker/date unique key keeps only one row for 9 Mar 2026.
184445214585182.data: 61 pages with ~54 sourced chart and table captions; only about 2 GEV-specific pages.
184445214585182.event: Written after 4Q25, with the target set 10 Dec 2025. No GEV deal or regulatory event cited.

214512485518521.why: Overweight, Top Pick; PT $775 (no revision shown; 23X the average of $34/$35 '27/'28 EPS). The core moat is still compounding — 3.6bn DAFU, 2bn Instagram DAUs — and the 3Q guide's $64bn top end implies 26% y/y ex-FX, an acceleration on a two-year stacked basis (51% in 3Q vs 48% in 2Q). Management said "soon" 12 times on the call about product updates, and MS sizes four call options — neocloud $2.97, Meta AI Search $2.89, subscriptions $1.88, API $1.22 — worth up to $9 (~25%) on its $34.59 '28 EPS; realizing half alone puts the stock at ~14X '28. MS '27/'28 EPS rose +2%/+4%; revenue '26 $255.9bn, capex $144.7bn '26 rising to $250bn '28, with FCF negative in '27 (-$26.2bn).
214512485518521.insight: Mostly restated 2Q commentary plus MS modeling; the one original artifact is the 4-product sizing from its 2 Jun 2026 note. No channel checks or survey.
214512485518521.data: Prior-vs-current model table, full income statement/balance sheet/cash flow, the call-option EPS bridge, risk-reward with options-implied probabilities.
214512485518521.event: Around the 2Q print (Jul 29 close $585.61), with Meta Connect (Sep 23/24) framed as the next catalyst.

584115845522224.why: Overweight, Top Pick; PT $775 (unchanged). Muse, META's standalone consumer AI agent (ex-"Hatch"), opens the $30tn consumer agentic TAM MS maps across retail/travel, ads, AV/rideshare, delivery, logistics and wearables. It handles shopping, travel, tickets, scheduling and email; purchases need user verification; it is a separate app that does not yet feed META's ad system. MS argues scaled distribution plus unique social datasets (FB/IG/Messenger/WhatsApp, even Gmail) and a free entry price give META an edge, with the Watermelon model due this Fall. The mechanism is unpriced optionality: META trades at 18X '28 EPS, and MS '26 EPS of $31.80 sits only marginally above consensus $31.41, with '26 constant-currency growth of 26.6%.
584115845522224.insight: Analyst hands-on use of the launch product and MS's own $30tn TAM framework, but no survey, channel check or n=; largely a framing piece with a GOOGL read-across.
584115845522224.data: TAM exhibit ($29tn 2023 → $32tn 2028), Muse integration screenshots, plus two risk-reward pages (META and GOOGL $400 PT).
584115845522224.event: The day after the Muse launch (Sep 8 close $613.48); explicitly a "what matters next" watchlist, since FB Shopping, the Metaverse and MetaAI disappointed.

585544818582814.why: Overweight, Top Pick; PT $775 (below the $825 in MS's 15 Mar 2026 note in this batch). Muse Spark (ex-"Avocado"), META's first homegrown model out of Meta Superintelligence Labs, is the "first step in re-rating." Benchmarks sit slightly below leading models but the gap is smaller than investors feared, so META's edge shifts to productization: shopping mode is already live with multi-modal, reasoning-driven shoppable links drawing on META's user/influencer content, which MS thinks lifts conversion where trust is the gating factor. Muse Spark is closed source but offered via API to select partners, so API revenue is "not priced at 17X '27 EPS." META trades at 17x '27 EPS ($36.3, 16% '25-'27 CAGR) and 1.1x '27 PEG versus a 2.4x peer median — a ~54% discount; the $775 PT implies 21x '27 and still a ~42% PEG discount.
585544818582814.insight: Analysts' own hands-on product trial plus MS's recurring surveys/trackers (trust gating agentic purchase adoption) — semi-proprietary, no new n= disclosed.
585544818582814.data: Shopping-mode screenshots, NTM P/E history chart, PEG comp table vs AAPL/MSFT/GOOGL/AMZN/NFLX, DCF (8% WACC, 3% terminal).

184444528445552.why: Overweight; PT $825 (11x '27 EBITDA, implying ~23x '27 EPS; PT averages a multiples valuation $806 and DCF $844 at 8% WACC / 3% terminal growth). Weekend media reports that META plans to cut ~20% of staff (~16k) could yield $3bn-$13bn of savings at $200k-$800k per head, i.e. 3-11% upside to MS's '27 EBIT (text says 5-10%) — and headcount costs are ~80% of META's opex ($131bn of $165bn total opex in '26E). Management's own line: META saw a "30% increase in output per engineer since the start of 2025, with the majority of that growth coming from adoption of agentic coding." MS frames this as offsetting accelerating GenAI capex/opex, lifting the near-term EPS floor while preserving long-term torque. Bear/base/bull PTs $500/$825/$1,100 on base '27 EPS of $36.63.
184444528445552.insight: No proprietary data — it aggregates media reports (XYZ -40%, ORCL, ADSK -7%, AMZN) and MS's own opex-per-head math, cautioning against using the ~$1.2mn ex-D&A opex per employee as the savings rate.
184444528445552.data: Three exhibits — headcount-cost build, RIF sensitivity table, full multiples-plus-DCF PT build.
184444528445552.event: Triggered by a weekend press report on job cuts; no print, no deal.

812844241442842.why: Overweight, PT cut to $750 from $820 (bull $1,000, bear $450); implies ~23x '27 EPS, 12% upside to the $650.13 close (10 Dec 2025). Three catalysts. (1) Revenue revisions — MS is 2%/4% ahead of Street for '26/'27. (2) A '26 opex "clearing event": MS raises '26/'27 GAAP opex 5%/6% to $155bn/$187bn and capex to $115bn/$135bn, cutting '26/'27 EPS ~8%/8% to $29.35/$33.02; the point is a credible floor of ~$30/$33 EPS that starts tactical buying at ~22x NTM (down from ~28x earlier in '25, vs GOOGL's 33% premium, a 3-yr high). (3) Superintelligence-team model/product nodes — a frontier model (likely Blackwell-trained) possibly this spring; success drives the $1,000 bull case at ~27-28x.
812844241442842.insight: Proprietary bottom-up opex model (hyperscaler deals, D&A, energy, headcount), not channel checks; no survey n=.
812844241442842.data: NTM P/E history, the opex build table, bull/base/bear valuation splitting multiples and DCF (8% WACC, 3% terminal), growth-adjusted comp table, full prior-vs-current model, risk-reward with options-implied probabilities (29.5% >$750, 17.7% <$450).
812844241442842.event: Pre-print — positioned ahead of the January 4Q opex guide, with sentiment explicitly negative.

412424458858248.why: Overweight, Top Pick, PT $775 (unchanged; bull $1,000, bear $450), 37.6% upside to the $563.29 close (30 Jun 2026), ~23x '27 EPS of ~$34. Written on a Bloomberg report that Meta plans a cloud business (a Bedrock-like hosted API serving Muse models, plus a raw-silicon neocloud offer) inside Meta Compute. MS argues the neocloud half is the easy half: META brings on ~2GW/~3.5GW owned-operated IT capacity in '26/'27 on a ~3GW YE25 base while renting ~2.5GW from Coreweave/Nebius/GCP/ORCL, versus AMZN/GOOGL adding 5GW/9GW in '27. Modelling: every 250MW leased for one year at $40/W is ~$3 (8%) of '28 EPS; the whole sensitivity grid runs $1.49-$11.88 EPS (4-33%). A full hyperscaler API is a "show me" — Muse scored poorly on TerminalBench and SWE Bench Verified, and META lacks enterprise GTM. Capex modelled at $175bn/$205bn in '27/'28 vs $145bn in '26.
412424458858248.insight: Proprietary capacity and $/Watt sensitivity model ("interactive Meta Neocloud model"), not consensus restatement.
412424458858248.data: Capacity-additions chart, two sensitivity tables, hyperscaler capex stack ($1.2tn '27), full bull/base/bear build, risk-reward page.
412424458858248.event: Same-day reaction to a press report; META had not commented.

184152881185882.why: Overweight, Top Pick, PT $775 (~30% upside to the $600.47 close of 1 Jun 2026); bull $1,000 (28x '27), bear $450 (14x). Four products, each worth $1-3 to '28 EPS on top of ~$35.79: Meta AI search $2.89, subscriptions $1.92, core ad upside $0.94, neocloud $2.97 → $38.76. Search: 1bn MAU × 1 query/day × 10% commercial rate at $0.30/query = $11bn revenue, 8% of '28 EPS, with sensitivities to $30bn+/20%+ EPS (GOOGL search is $225bn) — META's query/commercial rates are deliberately a fifth of GOOGL's. Subscriptions: Meta One tiers $7.99-$49.99, Instagram/Facebook/WhatsApp Plus $2.99-$3.99; 60mn subs at $10 ARPU ≈ $7bn revenue / ~5% '28 EPS. Core ads grow 21%/18% in '27/'28; 1% ad upside ≈ $3.5bn revenue / ~2.5% EPS. Neocloud: management said selling compute externally was "definitely on the table" at the 27 May shareholder meeting.
184152881185882.insight: Proprietary TAM-sizing models and sensitivity grids; references a leaked Meta ad deck.
184152881185882.data: 14 exhibits — EPS bridge, search/subscription/MW sensitivity tables, tier pricing table, valuation build.
184152881185882.event: Quiet patch, but anchored to the 27 May shareholder meeting and the All-America vote.

812454818812842.why: Overweight, Top Pick, PT $775 (unchanged, 25% upside to the $614.23 close of 15 May 2026); '27 EPS ~$34.16. A model refresh, not a new thesis. (1) A 10% headcount cut (~8K) effective May → $800mn one-time charge and ~$2bn/$3.5bn opex savings in 2H26/FY27, calibrated on the '22-'23 Year of Efficiency RIF (21K heads, ~$2.1bn charges, ~$100k/head) and ~$450k opex/head; reports of ~16K would add ~$3.5bn '27 savings, ~$1.20 EPS. (2) '27 net headcount growth cut from 5% to ~3.5% after 6,000 job postings closed. (3) '26/'27 capex raised 7%/6% (~$10bn each) to $144.9bn/$174.5bn, lifting '27 D&A 9%. Net: '26 EPS +3.7% to $32.83, '27 flat. The "backup safety valve": 4.4/3.9GW added in '26/'27 could be rented for $10-15bn a year, ~8% '28 EPS upside.
812454818812842.insight: Proprietary headcount-cost and cost-of-revenue models; social-media reports flagged as unconfirmed.
812454818812842.data: D&A/cloud-deal cost build, opex-per-head table, prior-vs-current bridge, bull/base/bear build.
812454818812842.event: Written the weekend after RIF reports, ahead of Meta Conversations (3 Jun) and Connect (23-24 Sep).

812241152554422.why: Overweight, META is the team's Top Pick (pecking order META, AMZN, GOOGL), PT $775 vs the 13-Apr close of $634.53 (+22.1%), ~23x '27 P/E; no PT revision shown. Consensus mean $846.35, and the bull/base/bear cases are $1,000 (~26x) / $775 / $450 (~14x). MS models 34%/28% y/y revenue growth in 1Q/2Q and 28%/21% for '26/'27 (FY26 revenue $256.7bn, ad revenue $250.2bn), but the new Nebius/CoreWeave cloud deals raise '27 cost of revenue ($25.9bn of cloud-deal CoR vs $1.1bn in '25) and cut '27 GAAP EPS ~6% to $34.19 from $36.31, with $2.4bn of annual NBIS expense and up to $5.4bn of incremental annual CoR; FCF falls 7% to $23.7bn. Headcount cuts are the offset: every 10% reduction could add $1-$2 of EPS.
812241152554422.insight: MS's own bottom-up model plus industry/company conversations; no channel checks or n= survey on META.
812241152554422.data: Prior-vs-current META model, PT build (multiples + DCF at 8% WACC/3% terminal) with consensus distribution, cloud-cost and opex builds, peer PEG table, two risk-reward pages. MS is 17% above consensus on '27 META capex ($164.9bn vs $141.2bn).
812241152554422.event: Pre-earnings, written into the GOOG/META/AMZN 1Q26 prints, with April branded-ad softness flagged.

585424181184514.why: Overweight / Top Pick, PT $775 (~23x '27 P/E), unchanged; consensus mean $825.72. META has no separate call beyond the templated risk-reward page. META's own capex adds 1.4 GW (2025) / 1.9 GW (2026) / 3.4 GW (2027); grossing up its external compute deals with CRWV/NBIS/ORCL/GOOGL/AMZN, MS estimates an effective ~4 GW in '26 and '27 — notable for a company with no hyperscale business, so the return depends on productizing models (the "MetaClaw" agent) and monetizing 1P data. META capex: $72.2bn (2025) to $144.9bn (2026E) to $174.5bn (2027E); $85bn, or 55%, of '26 capex is forward build for '27+ GW, the most forward-loaded alongside AMZN/MSFT (GOOGL only 10%). Roughly 75-80% of incremental '27 capacity is still NVIDIA; ~$25bn/yr of hyperscaler opex grosses to ~3 GW.
585424181184514.insight: Proprietary bottom-up cost-per-GW and GW models built with MS's semis/hardware teams, not restated consensus.
